## Materials and Methods

Full details are given in Supplementary Materials and Methods.

**Pipeline and reference panel.** A Nextflow workflow screened each library for papillomavirus reads with Kraken2 against a combined human/HPV database, typed positives against the complete PaVE reference set (`r stats$panel_n` sequences) by STAR alignment, and classified early versus late viral transcripts. Code and configuration are available as stated under Data availability.

**Cohort.** Public human RNA-seq runs were discovered through NCBI Entrez and assembled into a case/control design spanning productive controls (warts, condyloma), epidermodysplasia verruciformis, cutaneous neoplasia (cSCC, actinic keratosis), an unselected-skin null, and cell-line, engineered and non-permissive-tissue comparators. Tier assignment read curated SRA metadata, with a small override table correcting studies whose submitted metadata is absent or misleading. `r comma(stats$n_screened)` libraries were screened.

**Whole-library screening.** Every library was screened in full: no step subsamples reads and `fasterq-dump` was run without a spot limit. This matters because reads deposited from a coordinate-sorted alignment emerge from the SRA in reference order, placing unmapped, and therefore viral, reads at the end of the run. Reads reaching the screen were a median `r pp(stats$spot_med)`% of the SRA-reported spot count, with per-tier medians spanning `r pp(stats$spot_tier_lo)`% to `r pp(stats$spot_tier_hi)`%, so no tier was read less completely than another.

**Calling infection and productivity.** A reference was assigned when coverage breadth was at least 0.10 and mean depth at least 2. Every library, including negatives, was scored as papillomavirus reads per million (RPM). Productive infection required at least three L1 major-capsid reads, and a control-calibrated detection floor was set at the 5th-percentile RPM of non-cell-line productive controls (`r p1(stats$floor_rpm)` RPM).

**Confounder control and statistics.** Sequencing depth entered every model as log~10~ library size. Library-selection chemistry was recovered from SRA `LibrarySelection` and, where that field is generic, from library-construction protocol text, resolving `r pp(stats$chem_pct)`% of libraries. Integration was read from the E1:E2 transcript ratio and validated against virus-host junctions and an independent graded cervical series. Logistic regressions and Fisher exact tests were fitted in R, with Wilson intervals for proportions and a Bayesian re-analysis under weakly-informative priors as a robustness check.
